newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pekao bank boosts capital in merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pekao bank boosts capital in merger plan.

text.p: Poland's Bank Polska Kasa Opieki SA (Pekao SA) increased its share capital by 97.65 million zlotys through an issue of 244,125 new shares, the bank said in a statement.
The bank declined to give further details.

But banking sources said the capital increase was part of a plan to build a banking group led by Pekao SA and the issue would be paid for by the state treasury shares in the group's three other banks: Pomorski Bank Kredytowy (PBKS), Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy (PBG) and Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy (BDK).

The finance ministry -- which oversees the plan, aimed at grouping the Warsaw-based Pekao SA with three banks spun off the central bank in 1989 -- said it would give more details about the group's consolidation at a news conference on Wednesday.
The privatisation of the group, which controls about 20 percent of Poland's banking services market, is likely to take place in 1998.
The four banks had a combined balance sheet total of 37 billion zlotys in mid-1996 and own assets of nearly two billion zlotys, making the group the largest force on the Polish market.
